guarantees.claim: When wr_req is asserted, addr_align_err is asserted iff any of tl_i.a_address[1:0] bits are high, detecting a non-word-aligned write address.
When wr_req is not asserted, addr_align_err is forced to 0, regardless of tl_i.a_address.

assumptions.claim: wr_req is asserted only for write transactions, and during those transactions tl_i.a_address[1:0] carries the low bits of the transfer address.
assumptions.risk: If wr_req is asserted during read transactions, an alignment error could be wrongly flagged or missing, possibly causing spurious error responses or masking real misalignments.

formal_sketch.consequent: wr_req is asserted only for write transactions, and during those transactions tl_i.a_address[1:0] carries the low bits of the transfer address

uncertain_points.claim: Alignment checking is only implemented for write requests (wr_req). It is unclear whether read requests also require alignment checks per the comportability specification.
uncertain_points.cond: when a read transaction is active (no signal in this chunk)
uncertain_points.risk: Unchecked read misalignments could allow partial read of secrets or cause data corruption if downstream logic does not handle partial reads.

formal_sketch.antecedent: when a read transaction is active (no signal in this chunk)
formal_sketch.consequent: Alignment checking is only implemented for write requests (wr_req). It is unclear whether read requests also require alignment checks per the comportability specification

security_implications: addr_align_err signals a misaligned write address, potentially preventing partial writes to control/status registers. If error handling is incomplete or if reads are unchecked, a misaligned transaction could bypass access controls, corrupt secrets, or leak data. The write-only check exposes a possible gap for read-based attacks.
